newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power prices mostly steady.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Thursday, supported by strong natural gas prices but stalled by forecasts for milder weather this weekend, sources said.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Friday's delivery were discussed at $16.00-$17.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), as compared with the $15.75-16.75 range on Wednesday.
Off-peak, non-firm ECAR power for Friday delivery was quoted unchanged in the $12.50-$13.50 range.
The December ECAR market was in the $18.70 area, power marketers said.
Peak, non-firm power prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Friday were assessed at $16.00-16.50, a more narrow trading range than Wednesday's $16.00-$17.50 area.
Off-peak, non-firm MAIN electricity was discussed flat at $11.50.
Peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) were talked in the $15.00-16.50 range, compared with the $15.00 area seen on Wednesday.
Off-peak, non-firm MAPP electricity was again pegged at $8.00-$10.50 in sluggish trading.
IES Utilities' 538 megawatt (MW) Duane Arnold nuclear unit in Palo, Iowa, is scheduled to shut down on Friday for a 30-day maintenance outage.

However, MidAmerican Energy Co reported earlier today that its 515 MW coal-fired unit 3 at its Neal Generating Station in Iowa resumed operations yesterday following last weekend's shutdown to repair a leak in a boiler tube.
This should allow more power into the northern Southwest Power Pool (SPP) region, traders said.
In the (SPP), peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in the northern part was traded in the $16.50-17.00 range, as compared with Wednesday's $18.00-$19.00 range in the southern part.
Off-peak prices for firm power in the SPP were discussed in the $10.00-11.00 area, while on the Tennessee Valley System, prices failed to budge again from the $17.50 mark.
Also in SPP, firm deliveries for peak power in January/February 1997 were said to be around $21.35.
Natural gas prices in the Midwest region were stable today in the $2.17-2.20 per million British thermal units range.
Forecasters are calling for a continuation of cold temperatures on Friday throughout most of the Midwest, but the weather is expected to turn more seasonable by the weekend.
